brimNotice.ca_succession_transfer_in:
Securities transferred in from another custody account were detected ({n} rows).
They were recorded as «Adjustment» transactions because they have no matching cash movement: the assumption is that you already owned them at a different broker.
If that is the case, and that broker is tracked in LibreFolio, then when you import the other half of the transaction the system will offer to link the two and turn them into a «Securities transfer».
The rows in detail:
brimNotice.corporate_action: Missing inherited per-unit cost (WAC): enter the cost of a single unit, not the total, to import this row.
brimNotice.scalable_unreadable_rows: {count, plural, one {# row could not be read and was not imported} other {# rows could not be read and were not imported}}: a date, an amount, a currency, the shares or the security is missing.
brimNotice.scalable_fees_unknown: {count, plural, one {# row came} other {# rows came}} without the fee and tax details: the amount is the one Scalable shows, without separate fees or taxes. Export again with the option to include fees and taxes to get them.
brimNotice.scalable_open_partial: {count, plural, one {# order is filled in part and still open: it is not imported yet and will arrive executed with a later export.} other {# orders are filled in part and still open: they are not imported yet and will arrive executed with a later export.}}
brimNotice.scalable_reversal: {count, plural, one {# row reverses a transaction already booked and was not imported.} other {# rows reverse transactions already booked and were not imported.}} Check the reversed transactions and correct them by hand.
brimNotice.scalable_not_imported: {count, plural, one {# row was} other {# rows were}} not imported: security transfers, corporate actions and types LibreFolio does not read yet. Add them by hand if they move shares or cash.
brimNotice.scalable_several_overnight_accounts: The file holds {count} overnight accounts: all their rows go into this broker, whose balance is their sum.
brimNotice.scalable_internal_transfers: {count, plural, one {# transfer} other {# transfers}} between the broker account and the overnight account: import the other account's file into its own broker, then merge each pair into a Cash Transfer in the bulk editor.
brimNotice.scalable_dividends_net: {count, plural, one {# dividend was imported as credited} other {# dividends were imported as credited}}, net of the tax withheld: the file does not give the tax.
brimNotice.scalable_tax_refund: {count, plural, one {# tax refund was imported as a deposit} other {# tax refunds were imported as deposits}}: in LibreFolio a tax always takes money out.
brimNotice.scalable_cash_by_sign: {count, plural, one {# cash row has a type LibreFolio does not know, or an unexpected sign: it was recorded as a deposit or a withdrawal} other {# cash rows have a type LibreFolio does not know, or an unexpected sign: they were recorded as deposits or withdrawals}}, by the sign of the amount.
brimNotice.fineco_not_yet_settled: {count, plural, one {# row is not settled yet (its value date is after today) and was not imported: it arrives with the next export.} other {# rows are not settled yet (their value date is after today) and were not imported: they arrive with the next export.}}
brimNotice.fineco_incomplete_rows: This import may be wrong: {count, plural, one {# row lacks} other {# rows lack}} a required number (quantity or amount). Check the rows below; if the file is right, it is likely an importer bug, and you can help us fix it:
brimNotice.rows_not_recognized: {count, plural, one {# row was} other {# rows were}} left out, or only partly imported, because the importer does not recognise or does not yet import what {count, plural, one {it describes} other {they describe}}. Check the rows below; if this matters for your shares or cash, report it so we can handle the case:
brimNotice.rows_unreadable: {count, plural, one {# row was} other {# rows were}} left out because a value {count, plural, one {it needs} other {they need}} cannot be read. Check the rows below; if the file is right, report it so we can handle the case:
brimNotice.possible_split: Possible stock split of {ticker}: {added_quantity} new shares at no cost. Link a SPLIT event, or create one.

fixStep.intro: These rows were recorded, but the file did not say enough for the importer to be sure. Settle them now: the duplicate check that follows compares each row against your database, and a row filed under the wrong type is compared against the wrong things.
fixStep.pending: {n, plural, one {# row still to settle} other {# rows still to settle}}
fixStep.allDoneDetail: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing to correct.} one {# row settled. You can move on.} other {# rows settled. You can move on.}}
fixStep.acceptAsIsHint: Keeping it as recorded is a deliberate choice: the row is imported the way the importer filed it.
fixStep.acceptAll: {n, plural, one {Keep the remaining row as read} other {Keep the remaining # rows as read}}
fixStep.acceptAllHint: Accepts the plugin's reading for every row still waiting. You can still change any of them afterwards.
fixStep.groupTrades: Cash movements that may be operations
fixStep.groupTradesHint: Recorded as a deposit or a withdrawal because the file gives no quantity and no instrument. If they were a purchase or a sale, correct them now.
fixStep.groupSplitsHint: The file gives one amount for an operation that contains more than one: the price of the security, accrued interest, commissions. If you have the net countervalue you can split it here; otherwise keep the row as it is.
fixStep.groupCharges: Fees and taxes with no instrument
fixStep.groupChargesHint: Fees or taxes on securities operations that the file links to no instrument. Assign them to the right security, or keep them as they are if they concern the account.
fixStep.resetHint: Puts this row back the way the file was read, discarding the answer given here.
fixStep.resetAllHint: Puts every settled row back the way the file was read.
fixStep.splitTitle: Separate the price from the charges?
fixStep.splitNominalHint: The nominal value is the capital of the security — what the bank redeems at maturity — not what you paid. It was read from a coupon of the same security.
fixStep.splitLegsHint: Add one line per charge shown on your contract note. What is left is the price of the security: the legs always add back up to the row.
fixStep.splitErrorExceeds: The charges together exceed the {total} on the row: nothing would be left for the security.
fixStep.splitErrorNonpositive: Every charge needs an amount greater than zero.
fixStep.reportIssueHint: If a row keeps looking wrong, it may be an importer bug rather than your data:

warning.mixed_accounts_in_file: A securities export contains several custody accounts.

brimEvidence.scalable_unreadable_rows: On these rows a date, an amount, a currency, the shares or the security is missing or cannot be read.
brimEvidence.scalable_fees_unknown: The fee and tax columns are empty on these rows: unknown, not zero.
brimEvidence.scalable_open_partial: The shares column is what was executed so far; lf_ordered_shares is what was ordered.
brimEvidence.scalable_reversal: These rows are reversals: their lf_is_cancellation column is true.
brimEvidence.scalable_not_imported: The type column says what these rows are.
brimEvidence.scalable_several_overnight_accounts: The first row of each overnight account; the lf_account_index column tells them apart.
brimEvidence.scalable_internal_transfers: These rows move money between your two Scalable accounts (lf_subtype CASH_TRANSFER_IN or CASH_TRANSFER_OUT): each one has its twin in the other account's file.
brimEvidence.scalable_dividends_net: The tax column is empty on these rows: the amount is what reached the account.
brimEvidence.scalable_tax_refund: A positive amount in the tax column is money given back.
brimEvidence.scalable_cash_by_sign: The sign of the amount column decided between deposit and withdrawal.
brimEvidence.fineco_not_yet_settled: The value date of these rows is after today: they have not settled yet.
brimEvidence.fineco_incomplete_rows: The last column names the field without a number; the row is imported as it is.
brimEvidence.rows_not_recognized: The last column says what each row is, or what of it was not imported.
brimEvidence.rows_unreadable: The last column says what could not be read on each row.
